part2.question: Describe a time when you changed an important decision of yours

segments.v: I want to talk about a decision I changed in grade 9. At first, I decided to take the exam for the chemistry class at a specialised high school. Chemistry was my best subject and my parents liked this idea. I studied chemistry very hard for many months. But then I changed my decision. I did a practice test and I felt the exam was very difficult. The school was also very far from my house. My English teacher told me that I was good at English and I should choose the English class. I talked with my parents and they agreed. So I chose the English class at a public school near my house. I was worried because I studied chemistry for a long time. But now I feel happy because I like my class and I am not stressed. I think it was a good decision.

fluency.band6: Answers the bullets in order; mostly simple past; ends with a flat evaluation.
fluency.band9: Hook (the decision shaped the present) → original plan with reasons → three reasons for changing (First, Second, Third) → the change → feelings → a life lesson.

lexical.band6: decided, best subject, very difficult, far, happy, stressed.
lexical.band9: shaped, selective, keen on, prestigious, have second thoughts, mock exam, invested, take the easy way out, source of stress.

grammar.band6: Error: “because I studied chemistry for a long time” needs past perfect (I had studied).
grammar.band9: Past perfect (I'd decided; I'd already invested), past perfect continuous (who'd been training since grade 6), mixed conditional thinking (even if I got in, I'd be competing…), and gerund subject (changing your mind isn't a sign of weakness).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 has a tense error: “because I studied chemistry for a long time” should be past perfect (“I had studied”), since it happened before the change. Band 9 organises three reasons with First/Second/Third and ends with a life lesson.
